prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Checkout A/B Test Results (language en).
Grid: 7 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Metric" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Control" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Variant" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Lift" spans 1 col × 2 row; "p-value" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Metric" · longest unbreakable word 100px · one-line width 263px
  col 2: header "Control › Mean" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 52px
  col 3: header "Control › 95% CI" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 113px
  col 4: header "Variant › Mean" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 50px
  col 5: header "Variant › 95% CI" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 110px
  col 6: header "Lift" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 52px
  col 7: header "p-value" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 55px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare checkout outcomes for the control and variant, including uncertainty, relative lift and statistical significance.","reading":"Readers scan each metric across its row, comparing the two means and confidence intervals before checking lift and p-value. Longer metric labels can use multiple lines; the two-tier header already occupies extra height.","groups":["Control Mean and 95% CI belong together as the estimate and its uncertainty; Variant Mean and 95% CI play the same roles and should have comparable widths.","Lift and p-value are compact summaries of the comparison for each metric.","Metric labels identify the row and anchor the comparisons across it."],"keep_intact":["Individual means, percentages, currency amounts, p-values and lift values.","Time values and numeric identifiers such as 1,000.","Confidence intervals where space permits, especially the time and currency intervals."],"may_wrap":["Metric labels at word boundaries.","Confidence intervals at natural break points if needed, keeping each endpoint intact.","The p-value header if its column is too narrow."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [210, 73, 108, 71, 107, 73, 77] · table 720×420px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 36, 60, 36, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/9 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [160, 73, 134, 71, 131, 73, 77] · table 720×467px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 36, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/9 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [200, 73, 115, 71, 110, 73, 77] · table 720×444px · row heights [36, 36, 60, 60, 36, 60, 36, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/9 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
